# Management Access (RADIUS, TACACS+, Users, SSH)

_Extreme Fabric Engine · 20 commands_

Who may log in and how. RADIUS for CLI/web login and for NAC, TACACS+, local users, SSH and banners, including the exact `no` forms to remove each piece. Step by step removal and re-adding is in the change workflows (`ncs list flows`).

## Details

### `show radius`

The servers themselves are in `show radius-server`. Every server entry is one row per host and `used-by` (cli, eapol, web, snmp, endpoint-tracking), so the same IP can appear twice.


### `radius enable`

```
radius enable
radius accounting enable
no radius accounting enable
no radius enable
```

`no radius enable` switches RADIUS off but keeps every server entry in the config. To get rid of the servers, remove each one with `no radius server host <ip> used-by <app>`.

> ▲ **Caution:** With NAC in use, `no radius enable` stops all EAP/NEAP authentication on the switch.


### `radius accounting enable`

```
radius accounting enable
no radius accounting enable
```


### `radius server host <ip> key <secret> used-by cli [priority <1-10>] [timeout <1-180>]`

```
radius server host 10.0.0.50 key <secret> used-by cli priority 1
radius server host 10.0.0.51 key <secret> used-by cli priority 2
radius enable
```

`used-by` defaults to cli. The host can also be an FQDN or IPv6 address. Use `used-by web` for EDM/web login. Default priority is 10, so set it explicitly on every server to get a defined order.

> ▲ **Caution:** Test a RADIUS login from a second session before you close the one you are working in.


### `no radius server host <ip> used-by {cli | eapol | web | snmp | endpoint-tracking}`

```
show radius-server
no radius server host 10.0.0.50 used-by eapol
no radius server host 10.0.0.50 used-by cli
no radius server host 10.0.0.50 used-by eapol acct-enable
```

There is no command that removes all RADIUS servers at once, and `no radius enable` keeps them. Remove each row of `show radius-server` with its host and used-by. Adding a keyword after used-by only switches that option off (the last example disables accounting for that server and keeps the entry). `default radius server host <ip> used-by <app> <option>` resets one option (timeout, retry, port, ...) to its default.


### `no radius dynamic-server client <nac-ip>`

```
show radius dynamic-server
no radius dynamic-server client 10.0.0.50
radius dynamic-server client 10.0.0.60 secret <secret> enable
```

To only stop the client and keep the entry, use `no radius dynamic-server client <nac-ip> enable`. Check the result with `show radius dynamic-server [statistics]`.


### `radius cli-profile`

```
radius cli-profile
no radius cli-profile
```


### `tacacs server host <ip> key <secret> [port <1-65535>] [timeout <10-30>] [single-connection]`

```
tacacs server host 10.0.0.70 key <secret>
tacacs server secondary-host 10.0.0.71 key <secret>
tacacs authentication cli
tacacs protocol enable
```

Only a primary and a secondary server exist. In the 8.9 User Guide, TACACS+ falls back to the local users only when no server is reachable. An access-denied answer stops the login without trying local.

> ▲ **Caution:** Keep a second session open and test a TACACS+ login before you log out.


### `no tacacs server <ip>`

```
show tacacs
no tacacs server 10.0.0.70
no tacacs server 10.0.0.71
```

Created with `tacacs server host` or `tacacs server secondary-host`, but removed with `no tacacs server <ip>` for both. `default tacacs server <ip> {port | timeout | single-connection}` resets one option.


### `tacacs protocol enable`

```
tacacs protocol enable
no tacacs protocol enable
```


### `tacacs authentication {cli | web | all}`

```
tacacs authentication all
no tacacs authentication web
```


### `tacacs accounting enable cli / tacacs authorization enable`

```
tacacs accounting enable cli
tacacs authorization enable
tacacs authorization level all
no tacacs authorization enable
no tacacs accounting cli
```

With command authorization on and the server lost, a TACACS+ user can only run `exit` and `logout` (8.9 User Guide).

> ▲ **Caution:** Switch on authorization last, after a test login works.


### `username add <name> level {ro | rw | rwa} enable`

```
username add netops level rwa enable
username netops level rw
no username netops
```

Change the level later with `username <name> level <l1 | l2 | l3 | ro | rw | rwa>`. Delete with `no username <name>`, or only disable it with `no username <name> enable`. With enhanced secure mode the commands are `password create-user` and `password delete-user` instead.


### `cli password <login> {read-only | read-write | read-write-all | layer1 | layer2 | layer3}`

```
cli password rwa read-write-all
```

Out of the box each level has login and password equal to its name (rwa/rwa, rw/rw, ro/ro, ...). Check them with `show cli password`.

> ▲ **Caution:** Default logins on a production switch are a finding in every audit. Change them during commissioning.


### `ssh`

```
ssh
no ssh pass-auth
```

`boot config flags sshd` is the boot-time switch for the same daemon. Turn telnet off with `no boot config flags telnetd`. Password logins can be turned off with `no ssh pass-auth` once key login works.

> ▲ **Caution:** `no ssh` over an SSH session ends your own access: do it from the console or another method.


### `banner motd <text> / login-message <text>`

```
banner motd "Authorized access only"
banner displaymotd
no banner motd
no login-message
```

The MOTD only shows when `banner displaymotd` is set. `show banner` shows the current texts.
